status: UNREGISTERED DRAFT, not a gate protocol: no measured run may cite it and no decision may rest on it. Registration = review by the main session/user, then a copy to evidence/gsp05-v1-protocol.json with source commit, server/app manifest, image ids, harness sha256 and plan sha256 filled in, committed before the first measured run. Every parameter below is a proposal.
item: SP05/b tracker circuit breaker. C0 = legacy (indexer_breaker_threshold 0, today's behaviour); C5 = candidate (threshold 2, cooldown 120 s, doubling up to 600 s; UX/SLO frame row 4, user decision 2026-11-09).

source.manifest_method: sha256 over 'path:git-blob-id' lines of git ls-tree -r HEAD server/app (as gsp02-v4)
source.candidate_contents: feature/stream-performance + SP05/b (IndexerHealth in server/app/modules/indexers/search.py, config indexer_breaker_*; default 0 = legacy).

harness.what_is_real: API-key/DB auth, Stremio/provider/repository path, IndexerSearchService (per-tracker timeout, tracker cache, SP05/b breaker), shared source search (singleflight, 15 s deadline, .torrent download/store), Tech Info enrichment, filter/sort/serialization.
harness.what_is_synthetic: tracker adapters (per-indexer latency, timeout, connection error, flapping), .torrent download latency, nCore-like Tech Info stub. No real tracker, account or network; external HTTP is blocked and counted.

arms.switch_note: The harness applies the policy in-process (--policies legacy|candidate) on the same C image; the env column is the equivalent production setting.
arms.A_B_references: Descriptive only, proposal N/A: upstream and fork main lack the SP05/a timeout constant, so the harness refuses time scaling there and would need --time-scale 1 (see open_questions).

plan.runner: TBD by the gate runner: inside the C image, fresh disposable container and volume per run, 2 CPU / 1 GiB (as burst27/gsp02), sequential arms, order rotated per repetition (C0a,C5,C0b / C5,C0b,C0a / C0b,C0a,C5 ...).
plan.cold_warm: cold = fresh IMDb id per request (tracker cache, stored .torrent, stream response cache all cold); warm = same id right after, user's stream response cache invalidated. Reported separately; no warm-up request is part of a sample.
plan.time_scale_note: 0.25 scales every duration (12.5 s timeout -> 3.125 s, 15 s deadline -> 3.75 s, cooldowns, latencies, interval, flap periods) except the product's fixed 1.5 s Tech Info budget; reported numbers are unscaled. Estimated wall time ~6 min per legacy arm and ~4 min per candidate arm for S1-S4, ~20 min per repetition incl. container start, ~3.5 h for 2 x 5 repetitions.

decision_rule.primary_metric: S2 cold steady_latency_ms.p50 (cold requests with index >= --steady-from, i.e. after the breaker can have opened; the same window for every arm).
decision_rule.aggregation: per arm and series: median over the 5 runs of the per-run value.
decision_rule.noise: J(metric, scenario, kind) = max(|median C0a - median C0b| in the same series, resolution); resolution 50 ms (unscaled) for latency, 0 for counts and rates.
pass_if_all: S2: in BOTH series, C5 cold steady p50 < min(C0a, C0b) cold steady p50 - J.
S1 and S3: in both series, |C5 - C0a| <= J and |C5 - C0b| <= J for cold and warm steady p50 and p95.
S1 and S3: every C5 source_digest equals the C0a/C0b digest for the same (scenario, kind, index), and sources == trackers x results-per-tracker.
S3: C5 breaker openings == 0 in every run (slow but answering never opens).
S2: C5 healthy_sources >= C0 healthy_sources and C5 steady_partial_rate <= C0 (no loss on the answering trackers).
S2: C5 steady skipped_rate > 0 (the skip is visible as a warning stream, UX row 4).
All arms: external_http_attempts == 0, every request HTTP 200, no traceback with an application frame.
descriptive_only: S4 (flapping): sources lost while the tracker is up but still skipped, cold/warm p50/p95, subject requests per minute. The plan sets no S4 acceptance criterion.
decision_rule.otherwise: FAIL: indexer_breaker_threshold stays 0 (legacy). The FAIL is kept; a new version gets a new number.

open_questions: Run time: --time-scale 0.25 x 24 requests is ~3.5 h for 2 x 5 repetitions; 0.1 would be ~1.5 h but makes product overhead (DB, parsing) 10x larger in unscaled units. Which one?

Noise rule: this draft follows the plan text (medians, J from two baselines). gsp02-v1..v3 showed that rule under-estimating noise; should GSP05 use the gsp02-v4 bootstrap/Holm decider for the S1/S3 'unchanged' tests instead?
S4: descriptive only, or a guard (e.g. healthy sources unchanged and subject sources lost <= X %)? The breaker keeps skipping a tracker that came back until the cooldown ends.
A/B: report N/A, or run them descriptively at --time-scale 1 (needs a harness compatible with their provider signature)?

Partial-result effect: with 0.2 s downloads the legacy S2 deadline is not reached (partial_rate 0 in the smoke). Add a cell with slower downloads / more results (e.g. --download-latency 1.0 --results-per-tracker 10) to measure the 2.5 s tail the plan describes?

Implementation semantics to confirm: an answered error (auth, parse, HTTP status) resets the consecutive-failure count and closes after a probe; tracker-cache hits are still served while the breaker is open (no network call, no warning).

smoke_evidence.note: Wiring smoke only (is_measurement false), Windows host, in-process, while gsp02-v4 ran; not a measurement.
smoke_evidence.observed: 8 runs (legacy, candidate x S1-S4), 0 external HTTP attempts, ~13 s wall; S2 candidate opened once after 2 timeouts and then skipped with the warning text; S3 never opened.
